column1: # ELLA LEIBHOLZ, FOUND IN THE WRONG BOROUGH ON THE SAME DAY AS CHARLOTTE.
# Landesarchiv Berlin, Standesamt Tiergarten, P Rep. 820 Nr. 37, Namensverzeichnis zum Sterberegister 1974,
# page 67. Found 8 October 2026 in the West Berlin sweep. Confirmed at the image.
# THE SECOND OF THE FOUR. Work list row 245 named four Leibholz women who leave this archive's story with
# no death recorded — ELLA, CHARLOTTE, AGNES and ERNA. TWO OF THEM WERE FOUND IN ONE AFTERNOON, both in
# boroughs nobody had a reason to open. This is the stronger of the two.
field
*** LEIBHOLZ geb. BAESLER · ELLA JOSEPHINE MARTHA · 22. 6. · 1160 · ev. ***
column2: STERBEREGISTER TIERGARTEN 1974 NR. 1160, died 22 JUNE 1974, evangelisch. Typewritten, between LEIBER verh. Neumann and LEIDER verh. Lüdtke — the exact alphabetical slot. Crop at site/public/ella-leibholz-tiergarten-1974.png.

column1: and LEIBHOLZ IS AGAIN THE MARRIED NAME
column2: geb. Baesler. As with Charlotte geb. Schötzow in Tempelhof, the woman was born something else and married into the surname. TWO FOR TWO, which is worth noticing: if the Berlin Leibholz women of this generation married IN rather than being born to the name, then searching birth registers for them is the wrong instrument and always was.

column1: # ---------------- WHY SHE IS THE STRONGER CANDIDATE OF THE TWO ----------------
WHAT THE ARCHIVE HOLDS ABOUT ELLA
column2: LEIBHOLZ ELLA, KRANKENSCHWESTER — a nurse — in the Berlin directories from 1938 to 1970. SCHÖNEBERG, Dominicusstraße 43 in 1957 and 1959; WILLMANNDAMM 3 by 1964 and still there in 1967; present in the 1970 volume and gone after it.

column1: *** AND HER OWN BOROUGH WAS EXHAUSTED LOOKING FOR HER. ***
column2: ALL TWENTY-FIVE SCHÖNEBERG DEATH-INDEX VOLUMES FOR 1970-1994 were read on 21 September expressly to find her, every one bracketed on both sides, and the only name of the family's letters in the whole run is Erna Frida Else LEIPHOLZ in 1975. Row 245 recorded the result plainly: "ELLA DID NOT DIE IN SCHÖNEBERG IN THE TWENTY-FIVE YEARS AFTER SHE LAST APPEARS IN A DIRECTORY."

column1: THE GAP IS FOUR YEARS, NOT TWENTY
column2: she is in the 1970 directory and this entry is 22 June 1974. Compare Charlotte, who leaves the directory in 1967 and whose Tempelhof candidate died in 1982 — a fifteen-year gap. A SHORT GAP IS NOT PROOF, BUT IT LEAVES FAR LESS ROOM FOR A SECOND WOMAN OF THE SAME NAME TO HAVE LIVED AND DIED IN BETWEEN.

column1: and the ordinary explanation for the wrong borough is a hospital
column2: Row 253 wrote the caution before any of this was found: a person "may have moved, entered a home in another borough, or DIED IN A HOSPITAL WHOSE DISTRICT REGISTERED THE DEATH". A death registers where it happens, not where the dead person lived. ELLA WAS A NURSE; Tiergarten held large hospitals; Willmanndamm is a short way south of the borough line. NONE OF THAT IS EVIDENCE AND ALL OF IT IS ORDINARY.

column1: *** WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED ***
column2: that this is the Ella of Willmanndamm. The join is a surname, a forename and a bounded gap — exactly the material this archive got the Bloom mariner wrong on. "Josephine Martha" and "geb. Baesler" are new and check against nothing held here.

column1: WHAT SETTLES IT
column2: Sterberegister Tiergarten 1974 Nr. 1160. A 1974 entry gives the birth date, the birthplace, the LAST ADDRESS and the marital status. IF THE ADDRESS IS WILLMANNDAMM 3 THE QUESTION CLOSES. Orderable by number through service.berlin.de. *** A PURCHASE, AND DAVID'S TO MAKE. *** Note that this one and Tempelhof 1982 Nr. 161 are two separate offices and two separate orders.

column1: and unlike Charlotte, a free test may still exist for Ella
column2: Charlotte is in NO Berlin telephone book in any year, so the directories can never place her. ELLA IS DIFFERENT: she is in the printed directories from 1938 to 1970, a thirty-two year run, and the Schöneberg ADDRESS BOOKS and the house listing for Willmanndamm 3 have not been read year by year for her the way the telephone slot was read for Agnes. A 1971-1974 entry at a TIERGARTEN address would join the two women without paying for anything.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT THE TWO FINDS TOGETHER DO TO THE METHOD ----------------
*** THE SWEEP'S PREMISE IS NOW DEMONSTRATED TWICE OVER ***
column2: the archivist's letter of 29 September says there are 150+ Standesämter in Berlin and NO NAME INDEX ACROSS THEM. That is precisely why "she moved to another borough" has sat unanswerable in four work list rows for weeks. BOTH WOMEN TURNED UP IN BOROUGHS THAT WERE ON THE LIST ONLY BECAUSE THEY ARE AMONG THE TWELVE OF WEST BERLIN — Tempelhof and Tiergarten were not connected to anybody by anything. Reading a borough because it is there, rather than because a lead points at it, is what found both.

column1: AND THE HOME-BOROUGH NEGATIVES WERE NOT WASTED
column2: Schöneberg's twenty-five volumes and Neukölln's twelve are what make these two candidates worth anything. Without the exhaustive negative next door, a Leibholz in Tiergarten is just another Leibholz.
